questions.q: What is the main difference between ethics and law in hospitality?
options: Ethics applies only to managers, law applies to all staff
Law sets the compulsory minimum enforced by the state, while ethics is wider and covers actions that may be legal but still wrong
Ethics and law always require exactly the same behaviour
Law is voluntary, while ethics is enforced by the courts
questions.explain: Topic 1: law is the minimum punished by the state; ethics is wider — for example, hiding fees in small print can be legal but unethical.

questions.q: Which reasons explain why ethics is especially important in hospitality?
options: Service is intangible and produced in direct contact with the guest
Staff have access to guests' rooms, belongings and personal data
Hospitality businesses are not regulated by any laws
Reputation spreads quickly through online reviews
questions.explain: Topic 1: intangibility, staff access to guests' property and data, and fast-spreading reputation make ethics central; hospitality is of course regulated by law.

questions.q: Which level of hospitality ethics deals with fair pricing, codes of conduct and the treatment of staff by a hotel?
questions.explain: Topic 1: the organisational level covers company decisions such as pricing, codes of conduct and staff treatment.

questions.q: A manager decides to overbook rooms because it keeps occupancy high and benefits most guests and the owners. Which ethical theory is this reasoning closest to?
questions.explain: Topic 2: utilitarianism (Bentham, Mill) judges actions by their consequences — the greatest good for the greatest number.

questions.q: Which philosopher is associated with the categorical imperative and duty-based ethics?
questions.explain: Topic 2: Kant's deontology says some actions are right or wrong in themselves; people must be treated as ends, never merely as means.

questions.q: Virtue ethics focuses mainly on the consequences of an action rather than on the character of the person.
questions.explain: Topic 2: virtue ethics (Aristotle) focuses on character — what a good, honest professional would do. Consequences are the focus of utilitarianism.

questions.q: When was the UNWTO Global Code of Ethics for Tourism adopted, and how many articles does it have?
questions.explain: Topic 3: the Code was adopted by the UNWTO General Assembly in 1999 (Santiago, Chile) and has 10 articles; the UN General Assembly acknowledged it in 2001.

questions.q: The Global Code of Ethics for Tourism is a voluntary document rather than a binding law.
questions.explain: Topic 3: the Code is voluntary; it guides governments, businesses, communities and tourists, and is promoted by the World Committee on Tourism Ethics.

questions.q: How does a code of conduct differ from a code of ethics?
options: A code of conduct gives concrete rules of behaviour, while a code of ethics states general values and principles
A code of conduct is written only for guests
A code of ethics is always longer and more detailed than a code of conduct
There is no difference; they are legal synonyms
questions.explain: Topic 3: a code of ethics explains the values (the 'why'); a code of conduct lists practical rules (what to do and not do).

questions.q: Which dimensions belong to the SERVQUAL (RATER) model of service quality?
questions.explain: Topic 4: RATER = Reliability, Assurance, Tangibles, Empathy, Responsiveness. Advertising is not a dimension.

questions.q: Giving a front-line employee the authority to solve a guest's problem without waiting for a manager is called…
questions.explain: Topic 4: empowerment lets staff react quickly to guest problems; Ritz-Carlton is a well-known example.

questions.q: Which characteristic of hospitality services means that an empty hotel room tonight cannot be sold tomorrow?
questions.explain: Topic 4: perishability — services cannot be stored, so unsold capacity is lost.

questions.q: Which grooming rule is typical for waiters in food service?
options: Strong perfume to create a pleasant atmosphere
Long decorated nails as part of the corporate image
Short clean nails, minimal jewellery and hair tied back
Personal clothing instead of a uniform
questions.explain: Topic 5: hygiene rules require short clean nails, little jewellery and neat hair; strong perfume spoils the dining experience.

questions.q: According to standard telephone etiquette, how should a hotel employee answer a call?
options: With a greeting, the hotel or department name, own name and an offer of help
Simply "Hello?" and wait for the caller to explain
With the guest's room number to save time
By putting the caller on hold immediately without asking
questions.explain: Topic 6: a professional answer includes greeting + hotel/department + own name + 'How may I help you?'.

questions.q: Which are elements of traditional Kazakh hospitality (qonaqjailylyq)?
options: Seating the most respected guest in the tör, the place of honour
A generous dastarkhan with tea, baursak and main dishes
Charging the guest for each cup of tea
Giving sarqyt — food to take home
questions.explain: Topic 7: tör, the dastarkhan and sarqyt are traditional elements; charging guests for tea contradicts the tradition.

questions.q: Ethnocentrism means judging other cultures by the standards of one's own culture and seeing it as superior.
questions.explain: Topic 7: ethnocentrism is a barrier to intercultural competence; staff should replace judgment with curiosity and respect.
